name: Tony Benn
role: British Labour MP, Cabinet minister and left-wing figure (1950-2001); President of the Stop the War Coalition (2001-2014)
summary: A democratic socialist and Christian socialist who moved left after serving in Labour cabinets, Benn argued for public ownership, industrial democracy, planning and import and capital controls, and for a republican, secular constitution with an end to the House of Lords and Crown prerogative. He opposed EEC membership, nuclear weapons and military action without UN authority, and worked within Parliament and the Labour movement rather than for revolution.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Argued for planned trade, state-directed investment and public control of industry over market outcomes.

public-ownership.rationale: Defended public enterprise as minister and opposition MP and opposed privatisation of coal, energy and electricity.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Attacked tax cuts for the rich in 1973 and the 1990 electricity sell-off as financing a tax cut for the rich.

unions-good.rationale: Defended unions as protecting members, backed the NUM in 1984 and criticised judicial and legal curbs on them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Argued for planning agreements and a public enterprise board to counter multinational companies and abuses of business power.

cut-welfare.rationale: Condemned the Thatcher government's spending cuts as favouring the strong over the weak.

worker-ownership.rationale: As Industry Secretary he backed the Meriden workers' cooperative and argued for industrial democracy and workers' self-management.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Criticised MI5 vetting and surveillance of political activity as protecting the status quo, while accepting scrutiny of spies and terrorists; wanted civil liberties set in statute.

strong-leader.rationale: Objected to the Prime Minister's use of Crown prerogative powers without Parliament and wanted power made accountable.

abortion-legal.rationale: Described the Corrie Bill, which sought to restrict abortion, as the biggest attack in years on women's rights.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Stressed UN Security Council authority over force and suggested ceding Falklands sovereignty to the UN, but also demanded national sovereignty over the EEC.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Opposed NATO bombing of Serbia and war on Iraq as lacking UN authority, while condemning ethnic cleansing; he did not rule out all intervention.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Supported nuclear power as Energy Secretary, but by the 1980s opposed it, and later called it neither cheap nor safe.

central-planning.rationale: Favoured democratic planning of trade and investment and a National Enterprise Board, but not Soviet-style comprehensive planning; evidence is mixed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Supported planned trade and import controls in 1981 while acknowledging real problems with them in 1979.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed redirecting pension funds, North Sea revenue and defence money into industrial expansion and backed the National Enterprise Board.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Said he had long been a republican and his Bill ended the constitutional status of the Crown.

democracy-best.rationale: Defended parliamentary democracy and argued that its core is open debate and a secret ballot.

direct-votes.rationale: Proposed a referendum on EEC entry and wanted constitutional questions put to the public, but also defended parliamentary democracy based on debate and secret ballot.

separate-church-state.rationale: His Bill would create a secular Commonwealth and disestablish the Church of England.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred: he wanted a secular state and a secular constitution, which is incompatible with basing law on scripture, though he was a practising Christian socialist.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Described a party test requiring belief in the dictatorship of the proletariat as undemocratic.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said he had always held that Israelis have the right to a national state, while insisting Palestinians also have one.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Stated that workers should have a far larger part in decisions in the firms where they work.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backed Irish reunification and the Palestinians' right to a state, and supported negotiable sovereignty over colonial remnants.

force-without-un.rationale: Argued that force against Iraq in 1990 and Serbia in 1998 without Security Council authority breached the UN Charter.

proportional-representation.rationale: Said he opposed proportional representation in some forms, especially list systems, and that it would not defeat the government; qualified rather than absolute.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said what is wrong in Britain is wrong at the top, where the powerful protect their privileges.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Argued that people should be citizens rather than subjects and that authority must answer to them.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Called judicial banning of a strike and sequestration of union funds a contemptible attack on trade unionism and defended unions' right to defend members.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposed EEC entry, led the case for withdrawal and called monetary union and a federal Europe a chimera.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Objected to ministers using royal prerogative to go to war and appoint officials without Parliament.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Stated Labour was committed to Irish reunification and that Britain must withdraw from Northern Ireland; his Bill ended British jurisdiction there.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Called for a national constitutional convention to reconsider the constitution as a whole and proposed a new constitution in his Bill.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Called for cancelling Trident and stopping Polaris.

common-currency.rationale: Opposed economic and monetary union as a chimera.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: His Bill provides for equal representation for women in elections.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: His Bill would abolish the House of Lords and personal titles; he campaigned to disclaim his peerage.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rejected a judge-enforced entrenched bill of rights as binding the living to the dead, though his own Bill set out fundamental rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: as a republican seeking to end hereditary titles and the Crown's status, he preferred rulers who are chosen over those who inherit.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Held that Parliament should be supreme but said it was not, because the Crown's prerogatives bypass it; his Bill ended the Crown's constitutional status.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: He and his wife became vegetarian in 1970 for ethical reasons.

corporate-influence.rationale: Pointed to abuse of business power, multinationals and ministers who later join company boards.

public-access-to-information.rationale: His Commonwealth Bill would amend the law on official information, and he attacked secrecy in the security services.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Wanted Parliament to override European law but cited the UN Charter as binding limits on British force.

defeat-communism.rationale: Argued for detente, coexistence and a nuclear-free Europe rather than confrontation with the Soviet bloc.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Voted for decriminalisation in 1967, later spoke against Section 28 and voted to equalise the age of consent and repeal Section 28.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: His Commonwealth Bill abolishes the offence of blasphemy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Backed industrial democracy and wider popular participation, and his Commonwealth Bill sought more direct citizen power.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: as a republican opposed to hereditary privilege he would reject succession of a leader by a child.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Argued that the powerful have protected their position and privileges at the top of British society.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Supported removing US nuclear bases from Britain and closing nuclear bases.

arms-reduction.rationale: Moved to cut British defence spending to the level of its European allies and attacked arms sales.

capital-controls.rationale: Criticised the 1979 end of exchange controls as accelerating plant closures and capital flight.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Backed a return to free collective bargaining over statutory pay boards.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Sought change through Parliament, open debate and elections and was a reformist, not a revolutionary.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Backed non-nuclear defence for Britain and unilateral cancellation of Trident and Polaris.

national-church-status.rationale: Wanted the Church of England disestablished and religions treated equally under law.

notes: Moved from technocratic modernism in the 1960s to workers' control and the Alternative Economic Strategy after 1970. Supported nuclear power as Energy Secretary (1975-79) and later opposed it. Evidence is drawn mostly from his Commons speeches; his books were not available as full text.
